scope: Read-only review of benchmark documentation, renderer, measured timing boundaries, retained raw data, archive identities and visual preview. Only this review file was written.
findings: No blocking issues or unsupported causal claims found. Historical Python-hosted figures and the current native-host cohort are distinguished.
All 60 chart labels match the retained native-host report in order and value. Both panels explicitly repeat the same native C cohort; precompiled runtime excludes preparation.
The previous V8/Python chart is byte-identical to the implementation-base commit. Archived chart and diagnostic-input bytes match their workspace sources.
Independently checked 400 archived phase outputs against goldens and raw timing records, all 50 phase summaries, 90 control observations and paired summaries, and 45 archived control timing files.
All 68 phase input hashes still match. Report, host-library, chart, preview and archive identities are consistent. The control lack of pre/post hashes is disclosed.
The retained PNG shows all ten example groups and 60 labels with legible legends and timing-boundary notes; no overlap was observed.
Sorting supports a substantial remaining execution-path gap. Life variation remains unexplained; the documentation avoids attributing it to instrumentation, frequency or a universal engine penalty.
limitations: No guest execution, performance sampling, build, test suite or renderer rerun was performed by this reviewer. Existing full host qualification and deterministic-render results were reviewed as retained evidence.
The phase probes are separate from headline measurements. Native main includes unbuffered stdout while Wasm entry excludes final host output delivery; neither is a pure compute kernel.
Control input hashes were recorded after collection only. The shared-host measurements do not isolate scheduling, frequency, layout or code-generation causes.
The final SHA256.json manifest is intentionally outside this review because it will be generated after this file.
